title: Value of the X-Hook-Secret handshake header
summary: A synthetic shared secret after the exact X-Hook-Secret header name in a raw handshake request, a quoted curl -H argument and a JSON header map, including a lowercase header name.
rationale: Asana sends the shared secret once, in the X-Hook-Secret header of the handshake request, and both sides then store it to verify later deliveries. The header is the carrier; Asana states no prefix, alphabet or width for the value, so the position is the only signal. The extent is the header value only.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#232). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Flagged under project policy: the value after the exact X-Hook-Secret header name is treated as a credential whatever its shape. Asana documents the header as the carrier of the shared secret (carrier existence only); the exact-name boundary, value admission, extent and a generic header attribution are the project's decisions. No alphabet or width is claimed.

sources.supports: Included in the header of that `POST` request from Asana is an `X-Hook-Secret`. This value serves as a shared secret that both Asana and the receiving server store.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. The carrier's existence is what the cited provider pages document; the value admission, span, placeholder handling and attribution are project policy. Parser behaviour, action and product attribution stay with the downstream repositories.
